newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa hires top beermaker as new crimebuster.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hires top beermaker as new crimebuster.

text.p: South Africa unveiled its latest weapon in the fight against crime on Saturday, announcing that one of the country's top businessmen has agreed to help run the police force.
Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said Meyer Kahn, group chairman of South African Breweries (SAB), would fill a new post as civilian chief executive of the police.
This would free national police chief George Fivaz of his administrative burden so he could concentrate on catching criminals, he told a news conference.

"Our selection of one of the private sector's toughest and ablest managers -- and his willingness to answer the call -- underscore the new era of partnership between the public and private sector to end the scourge of crime," Mbeki said.
President Nelson Mandela's government has made fighting crime a top priority, but has yet to convince residents -- and some foreign investors -- the situation is being brought under control.
The country has some of the world's worst rates of murder, armed robbery, car hijackings and rape.

Kahn's appointment for two years from August 1 is the latest of many initiatives, such as last week's lifting of a freeze on police recruiting, to combat crime and raise the poorly paid force's morale.
"Mr Kahn enjoys an international reputation for his successful leadership of one of South Africa's most dynamic and aggressive conglomerates," Mbeki said.

"With 105,000 employees and diverse operations in beer, hotels, retail and manufacturing, the SAB group approaches the South African Police Service in size and scope. In his nearly 31 years at SAB, Mr Kahn has turned the beer operation into one of the top four brewing companies in the world."

"His toughness as a manager is tempered by a common touch he has retained since his boyhood," Mbeki said. "His mischievous humour and blunt style will no doubt make for a smooth entry into the police service."
